findings.evidence: Moments.lean:36–37 `def count ... := (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => obs x = σ)).card` with no `@[expose]`; grep for `count_def|count_eq` in the PR yields only `signCount_eq_count`; Mathlib has no bundled fiber-count def, it uses `#{x ∈ s | f x = y}` directly (Mathlib/Combinatorics/Pigeonhole.lean:254, Mathlib/Algebra/BigOperators/Group/Finset/Basic.lean:993).
findings.fix: Add `theorem count_eq_card_filter (obs : X → S) (σ : S) : count obs σ = #{x | obs x = σ} := (rfl)`; optionally also `count_eq_zero : count obs σ = 0 ↔ ∀ x, obs x ≠ σ` alongside `count_pos`.
findings.issue: `count` has a hidden body (module, no `@[expose]`) and no restatement lemma; downstream cannot relate `count obs σ` to `#{x | obs x = σ}` and so cannot use Mathlib's fiber API (`Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise`, `Finset.card_filter`, pigeonhole lemmas) or prove e.g. `∑ σ, count obs σ = Fintype.card X`. Every other def in the PR has its restatement (`signCount_eq_count`, `signSum_eq_sum`, `fullMatrix_apply`, `fullInverse_apply`, `inverseCoeff_*`).

findings.evidence: Polynomial.lean:50 `@[simp] theorem signSum_eq_sum ... signSum Z p = ∑ x : Z, ...`; lines 70, 91, 100, 109 state the file's main results with `signSum Z (∏ j, Q j ^ ...)` on the left.
findings.fix: Keep `signSum_eq_sum` as the unfolding restatement but remove `@[simp]` from it.
findings.issue: `@[simp]` on `signSum_eq_sum` rewrites `signSum Z p` to its body, so `signSum` is never a simp normal form; the LHS of `signSum_product`, `signSum_prod_pow`, `fullInverse_signSum`, and `recovered_pos` is destroyed by `simp` before those lemmas can fire, and any downstream simp lemma about `signSum` (e.g. a Tarski-query identity) is unreachable.

findings.evidence: Moments.lean:154, 170 have no attribute; Mathlib marks `Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv`, `nonsing_inv_mul`, `mul_inv_of_invertible`, `inv_mul_of_invertible` `@[simp]` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/NonsingularInverse.lean:210–250).
findings.issue: `full_left_inverse` and `full_right_inverse` (`fullInverse J * fullMatrix J = 1`, `fullMatrix J * fullInverse J = 1`) are the normal-form inverse identities but carry no `@[simp]`, unlike Mathlib's corresponding matrix-inverse lemmas.

summary: Bodies are hidden and most definitions carry their restatement and entrywise lemmas, but `count` (the base definition every other count reduces to) has no `_def`-style lemma, so consumers cannot reach Mathlib's fiber-cardinality API, and `signSum_eq_sum` as `@[simp]` unfolds the definition that all the file's main identities are stated on.
